title: Sources of genetic variation in meiosis and fertilisation; Meiosis
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CD04#t3 term and clue written for the game; CD03#t3 term and clue written for the game; CD04#t4 term and clue written for the game; CD03#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CD03#N.3, CD04#N.6, CD03#N.10b, CD04#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Bivalent
items.clue: A pair of homologues joined together in prophase I

items.label: Meiosis
items.clue: The reduction division: one 2n cell gives four n cells

items.label: Chiasmata
items.clue: The points where non-sister chromatids break and rejoin

items.label: Haploid
items.clue: Having one set of chromosomes, as in a gamete; 23 in humans

questions.stem: A diploid nucleus of an organism with 2n = 14 undergoes meiosis. What is produced?

options.text: Four diploid nuclei, each containing 14 chromosomes
Four haploid nuclei, each with half of the organism's genes
Two haploid nuclei, each containing 7 chromosomes
Four haploid nuclei, each containing 7 chromosomes

questions.explanation: Two divisions give four haploid nuclei from one diploid nucleus. 2n = 14, so each has n = 7: one of each homologous pair.

questions.stem: Which statement describes crossing over during meiosis?

options.text: The two sister chromatids of one chromosome exchange their segments in prophase I.
At a chiasma, all four chromatids of a homologous pair exchange segments in prophase I.
Non-sister chromatids of a homologous pair exchange segments in prophase I.
Homologous pairs swap the sides of the plate they face at metaphase I.

questions.explanation: While homologues are paired in prophase I, non-sister chromatids exchange corresponding segments at chiasmata, making new combinations of alleles.

questions.stem: Which describes the cells produced when one spermatocyte, a diploid cell in the testis of an animal that is heterozygous for many genes, completes meiosis?

options.text: Two cells, genetically different from each other
Four cells, all genetically identical to one another
Two cells, genetically identical to each other
Four cells, each genetically different from the others

questions.explanation: One diploid cell gives four haploid cells. Each gets one homologue of every pair, and crossing over mixes alleles between chromatids, so in a heterozygous animal the four differ.

questions.stem: A mutation in a hypothetical species of animal prevents crossing over during meiosis, but meiosis is otherwise normal. Compared with the gametes of a normal individual, which prediction about the gametes of an individual with this mutation is correct?

options.text: Every gamete would be genetically identical, since crossing over is the only source of genetic variation.
They would vary less but still differ, because homologous pairs still orient randomly at metaphase I.
They would vary just as much as before, since crossing over just swaps sister chromatid segments.
Each gamete would carry either the full maternal or the full paternal set of chromosomes.
